edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. II, 6

source_text: Post haec sponsus loquitur: Ego flos campi et lilium convallium. Propter me, qui in valle eram, descendit in vallem et factus est lilium convallium. Sicut lilium inter spinas, sic proxima mea inter filias. Ego quidem flos campi; tu vero, ecclesia, lilium inter spinas — inter eos qui pungunt et tribulant. Flos campi Christus, qui in mundo patuit; lilium convallium, quia humilibus se praebuit.
pass_a_gloss: After these bridegroom speaks: I flower of-field and lily of-valleys. On-account-of me who in valley was, he-descended into valley and became lily of-valleys. As lily among thorns, so my neighbor among daughters. I indeed flower of-field; you however church lily among thorns — among those who prick and afflict. Flower of-field Christ who in world appeared; lily of-valleys because to-the-humble he-offered himself.
pass_b_english: After this the Bridegroom speaks: [[I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:1]]. For my sake, who was in the valley, he came down into the valley and became a lily of the valleys. [[As a lily among thorns, so is my neighbor among the daughters >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:2]]. I indeed am the flower of the field; but you, church, are a lily among thorns — among those who prick and afflict. Christ is the flower of the field, who appeared openly in the world; the lily of the valleys, because he offered himself to the lowly.
notes: Song Homilia II OET; Lawson not used for wording.
